title: MBR-BoN for Preference Dataset Curation in RLHF
summary: This paper applies MBR-BoN to generate preference datasets for RLHF, mitigating reward hacking by incorporating proximity regularization. The method uses Minimum Bayes Risk decoding to select diverse, high-quality responses, which are then used to train reward models. Experiments on Skywork-Reward-V2 and Anthropic's datasets show improved alignment and reduced overoptimization.
gap: Standard BoN sampling for RLHF datasets suffers from reward hacking due to imperfect reward models, limiting the quality of aligned policies.
approach: Extend MBR-BoN from decoding to preference dataset generation. Sample N responses per prompt, rank them using a reward model augmented with MBR's proximity term, and pair top-ranked responses with lower-ranked ones as preferences. Train reward models on this dataset and evaluate downstream RLHF performance.
evaluation: Compare datasets generated via MBR-BoN vs. vanilla BoN using Skywork-Reward-V2 metrics (AU-PRC, best-of-N scaling). Measure downstream policy performance via human evaluations on helpfulness/harmlessness.
